title: Florida House, District 32
what_it_does: Represents District 32 (Part of Brevard) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Brian Hodgers
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Insurance agency owner and realtor; state representative (elected in a June 2025 special election)
candidates.background: Hodgers, 53, of Viera, owns an insurance and real estate business and holds a business degree from Florida Atlantic University. He won a June 2025 special election to succeed Debbie Mayfield and describes himself as the only insurance agent in the Florida House.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted for HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), which would phase out all non-school property taxes on homesteads, and for HJR 1F (June 2, 2026), which placed the Amendment 3 homestead-exemption increase on the November ballot. He told News 6 he supports the amendment and told Vote411 property taxes are now the top concern he hears at the door.
property_tax.quote: providing meaningful property tax relief so families can afford to stay in their homes

insurance.summary: Says the 2023 litigation reforms stabilized the market and favors reducing fraud and increasing competition rather than more state intervention.
insurance.quote: Florida's 2023 insurance reforms have reduced excessive litigation and fraud, helping stabilize the insurance market.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)
2026 Voter's Guide - Florida House District 32, Republican primary (ClickOrlando / News 6)

healthcare.summary: Opposes expanding government programs, saying Medicaid should stay focused on the truly vulnerable and Florida should pursue market-based solutions.
healthcare.quote: Florida should prioritize sustainable, market-based solutions rather than expanding government programs.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)

abortion.summary: Describes himself as pro-life and supports abortion only when the mother's life is at serious risk or in cases of rape or incest, consistent with current law.
abortion.quote: I am pro-life and believe every human life is valuable and deserving of legal protection.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)

elections.summary: Supports requiring proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote, while backing fee waivers to make it accessible.
elections.quote: I support requiring proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote because protecting the integrity of our elections is essential.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)

housing.summary: Favors streamlining permitting and zoning and public-private workforce housing partnerships, but says the answer is more supply rather than government dependency.
housing.quote: The best long-term solution is to build more attainable housing, not create additional government dependency.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)
2026 Voter's Guide - Florida House District 32, Republican primary (ClickOrlando / News 6)

growth.summary: Supports maintaining the current balance in which the state sets uniform policy and local governments should not undermine state law.
growth.quote: Home rule should complement—not conflict with—statewide priorities.

sources.title: State Representative 32 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)

guns.summary: Voted for HB 133 (2026), which would lower the minimum age to buy a rifle or shotgun from 21 to 18; he is a lifetime NRA member.

environment.summary: Prioritizes the Indian River Lagoon and says more county sales-tax revenue should go to wastewater, septic and stormwater work.

energy.summary: Highlights his vote for a law preventing utilities from passing data-center costs to residential ratepayers.
energy.quote: Utility regulators should continue enforcing this law, protect residential ratepayers

candidates.name: Juan Hinojosa
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Security officer, Northrop Grumman; retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel
candidates.background: Hinojosa, 73, was born in Falfurrias, Texas, earned a biology and chemistry degree from Texas A&M-Kingsville and served 30 years in the Army, retiring as a lieutenant colonel in 2012. He lost the June 2025 HD 32 special election to Hodgers and now works as a security officer in Melbourne.
